summary: Find the single repeated number in an array of n + 1 values in [1, n] without modifying it and using O(1) space.
mainInsight: Treat the array as a function i -> nums[i]. Because there are n + 1 indices mapping into [1, n], a cycle exists and its entrance is the duplicate. Floyd's tortoise-and-hare finds the cycle, then restarting one pointer from the head finds its entrance.

approaches.name: Sort / set
approaches.summary: Sort and compare neighbours, or store seen values in a set.
weaknesses: Violates the space or no-modify constraint

approaches.name: Binary search on values (pigeonhole)
approaches.summary: Count elements <= mid; if more than mid, the duplicate is in [1, mid].

approaches.name: Floyd's cycle detection
approaches.summary: Find the meeting point inside the cycle, then advance from the head and the meeting point at the same speed.

commonMistakes: Starting the pointers at index 0 value and mixing indices with values
Forgetting the second phase after the pointers meet

promptVariants: Why does Floyd's cycle-detection algorithm solve Find the Duplicate Number?
How is the array turned into a linked list?
options: Following i -> nums[i] creates a cycle that enters at the duplicate
Equal values are adjacent after sorting, so a fast pointer finds them
Sorting the indices by value puts the duplicate next to its twin
Binary search halves the array so the duplicate is always the middle
cards.answer: Following i -> nums[i] creates a cycle that enters at the duplicate
cards.explanation: Two indices point to the same value, so some node has two predecessors, creating a cycle.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Equal values are adjacent after sorting,: The array is not sorted or modified.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Sorting the indices by value puts the du: Sorting would modify the array and cost extra time.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Binary search halves the array so the du: The duplicate is not necessarily in the middle.

promptVariants: Why does restarting a pointer from the start find the cycle's entrance?
What is the argument behind the second phase of Floyd's algorithm?
cards.answer: If the head-to-entrance distance is a and the meeting point is b steps past the entrance in a cycle of length c, then the fast pointer travelled twice the slow one: 2(a + b) = a + b + kc, so a = kc - b. A pointer from the head and one from the meeting point, both moving one step at a time, meet exactly at the entrance after a steps.
keyPoints: Both pointers meet at the entrance
cards.explanation: The entrance index value is the duplicate number.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
Why is the sort-and-compare approach not accepted here?
options: It modifies the array (sort) or needs O(n) extra space (set)
Sorting is slower than O(n), so it exceeds the time limit
It fails when the duplicate appears more than twice
It cannot find a duplicate larger than n / 2 in size
cards.answer: It modifies the array (sort) or needs O(n) extra space (set)
cards.explanation: The problem demands O(1) space and a read-only array.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Sorting is slower than O(n), so it excee: The time limit is not the issue; the constraints are.
incorrectOptionExplanations.It fails when the duplicate appears more: It handles repeats; the issue is the constraints.
incorrectOptionExplanations.It cannot find a duplicate larger than n: Values are not restricted that way.
